AUDIT QUESTION: Batch 84 cycle 2 = RULING 105, re-examined after cycle 1 (orchestrator 2026-11-14 '20:13', verbatim): "the hold exists because two INDEPENDENT readings disagreed on a number or name. Here the second recogniser disagrees WITH ITSELF on the same audio (one reading '401k', two '401'), while the decoder reads '401k' every time. A witness that changes its answer on identical audio is not evidence of a different word. So: when (1) the primary decoder's reading of the token is stable across its passes, (2) the second recogniser's repeated readings of the SAME audio differ among themselves and at least one equals the lock's token, and (3) every differing reading is a TRUNCATION of the lock's token (a prefix of the same term: '401' of '401k'), never a different number or name, the token is adjudicated as the lock's and the clip may seal. All readings are recorded on the pin ... under 'unstable_second_reading'. Anything else stays a final hold: a second recogniser that is stable in its disagreement, a different number ('68,000' / '86,000'), a different name. Must-fail tests for those three."
Context: pipeline/lock_precheck.py is the pin-stage pre-check; per segment it builds the lock, compares it with the second recogniser's long reading (rulings 72 / 84) and, on ONE number / name token, re-listens a short window with both recognisers (ruling 103). Each pass's answer is appended to results/<vid>.<start>-<end>.<decoder sha12>.json with the acquired source's source_file_sha256. Within one pass ruling 103 already decides; ruling 105's case is ACROSS passes (on Blockware the 13:51 pass read '401', a later pass under a new decoder sha read '401k' with no difference).
The change: pinned.truncation_of (the token minus a NON-DIGIT suffix only; a token without a digit, a name, never qualifies; an empty reading never does), reading_at (a long reading's token at the lock's token k by SequenceMatcher over the whole lock), reading_near (a SHORT window's token at k anchored on the lock's neighbours, because a whole-lock alignment can anchor a short window's edge words on the wrong part of the lock; "" when nothing anchors), unstable_second_reading (the three tests). lock_precheck._history: every earlier answer for the SAME span with the SAME source sha256 under any decoder sha (errors excluded); unstable(): no history -> None (ruling 103 alone decides, behaviour unchanged); else the lock's number / name tokens (never a negation) that any reading disputes; more than one -> hold; one -> the decoder readings (the lock + every re-listen's decoder reading) and the second readings (every long reading + every re-listen's second reading) at that token, judged by unstable_second_reading. In answer(): a current single-token hold whose re-listen held becomes "same" on a ruling-105 pass; a current agreement ("same" / "adopt") becomes "hold" on a ruling-105 hold (an earlier reading of this audio was no truncation). The entry records 'unstable_second_reading'; RULES adds 'ruling 105'.
Tests: TestRuling105 (7): the 401k history adjudicates as the lock's (agreeing now; and holding now); a stable disagreement holds; 68,000 / 86,000 holds even when it agrees now; a different name holds even when it agrees now; another audio is not history; the truncation rule. 48 passed; on the old files all 7 fail.
Cycle 1: qwen27b PASS; glm PASS with one note not agreed (a repeated anchor in a short window could read the wrong occurrence); closed anyway: reading_near now takes, of repeated anchors, the one nearest the reading's middle (the window is cut around the token), with a test; 49 passed.
FIND: anything cycle 1 missed: a fail-open (a number or name passing without all three tests true, or on another audio's readings); a negation or more than one disputed token adjudicated; a truncation that is really a different number or name; a change for a span with no history. Only state what you can verify from the diff. Reply with the JSON verdict; keep the reasoning short; at most 3 findings.

+    earlier one's) align on the whole lock, the short re-listen readings on the lock's tokens around the token. More

+    sec = seconds(k)
+    res = pinned.unstable_second_reading(L[k], [t for _, _, t in dec], [t for _, _, t in sec])

--- a/pipeline/pinned.py

@@ -429,6 +429,56 @@ def relisten_verdict(token, decoder_text, second_text):
     return "pass" if all(token in canon.canon_tokens(t or "") for t in (decoder_text, second_text)) else "hold"
 
 
+def truncation_of(token, other):
+    """RULING 105: `other` is `token` with only a NON-DIGIT suffix dropped ('401' of '401k'). Never a different number
+    ('680' of '68000'), never a name (a token without a digit: 'never a different name'), never an empty reading."""
+    return (bool(other) and other != token and token.startswith(other) and any(ch.isdigit() for ch in token)
+            and not any(ch.isdigit() for ch in token[len(other):]))
+
+
+def reading_at(lock_tokens, k, tokens):
+    """The reading's canonical token(s) at the lock's token k, aligned by SequenceMatcher: the lock's own token where
+    they match, the replacing token(s) joined where they differ, "" where the reading drops it."""
+    from difflib import SequenceMatcher
+    for tag, a, b, c, d in SequenceMatcher(None, lock_tokens, tokens, autojunk=False).get_opcodes():
+        if a <= k < b:
+            return lock_tokens[k] if tag == "equal" else " ".join(tokens[c:d])
+    return ""
+
+
+def reading_near(lock_tokens, k, tokens):
+    """A SHORT window's reading at the lock's token k (a whole-span alignment can anchor a short window's edge words
+    on the wrong part of the lock): the token itself if the reading has it, else the token right after the lock's left
+    neighbours in the reading (two words, then one), else right before its right neighbours; "" when nothing anchors
+    (fail closed: never a truncation)."""
+    if lock_tokens[k] in tokens:
+        return lock_tokens[k]
+    mid = (len(tokens) - 1) / 2                      # the window is cut around the token: of repeated anchors (audit
+    for n in (2, 1):                                 # batch 84 c1, glm), the one nearest the reading's middle
+        if k - n >= 0:
+            hits = [i + n for i in range(len(tokens) - n) if tokens[i:i + n] == lock_tokens[k - n:k]]
+            if hits:
+                return tokens[min(hits, key=lambda j: abs(j - mid))]
+    for n in (2, 1):
+        if k + 1 + n <= len(lock_tokens):
+            hits = [i - 1 for i in range(1, len(tokens) - n + 1) if tokens[i:i + n] == lock_tokens[k + 1:k + 1 + n]]
+            if hits:
+                return tokens[min(hits, key=lambda j: abs(j - mid))]
+    return ""
+
+
+def unstable_second_reading(token, decoder_readings, second_readings):
+    """RULING 105 (orchestrator 2026-11-14 '20:13'): the lock's token is adjudicated as the lock's only when (1) every
+    decoder reading of it gives it, (2) the second recogniser's readings of the SAME audio differ among themselves with
+    at least one giving it, and (3) every differing second reading is a truncation of it (truncation_of). Anything
+    else stays a final hold: a stable disagreement, a different number, a different name. Readings are the tokens at
+    the lock's place (reading_at). -> {"tests": {...}, "verdict": "pass" | "hold"}."""
+    tests = {"decoder_stable": bool(decoder_readings) and all(r == token for r in decoder_readings),
+             "second_unstable": token in second_readings and any(r != token for r in second_readings),
+             "truncations_only": all(truncation_of(token, r) for r in second_readings if r != token)}
+    return {"tests": tests, "verdict": "pass" if all(tests.values()) else "hold"}
+
+
 def _second_recogniser_words(src_path):
     """The independent second recogniser (ElevenLabs scribe_v1) on the acquired window: words on its clock."""

+    the lock's only when the decoder is stable, the second recogniser's readings differ among themselves with one
+    giving the token, and every differing reading is a truncation ('401' of '401k'). Must-fail (the order): a stable

+                        "as_spoken": {"text": heard}, "relisten": None}], f)
+
+    def ask(self, run, heard, decoder=None, second=None):
+        self.run_words, self.scribe_words = spread(run), spread(heard)
+        self.short_decoder = spread(decoder) if decoder else None
+        self.short_second = spread(second) if second else None
+        self.request("r105", approved_text=run)
+        LP.serve_once(log=self.log)
+        return self.entry(run)
+
+    def test_the_401k_history_adjudicates_as_the_lock(self):
+        self.past("I don't have a 401 ,")                          # 13:51: the second recogniser read 401
+        e = self.ask(self.RUN, self.RUN)                            # now it reads 401k: no difference
+        u = e["unstable_second_reading"]
+        self.assertEqual((e["outcome"], u["verdict"], u["token"]), ("no_difference", "pass", "401k"), e)
+        self.assertEqual(sorted(d["token"] for d in u["second_readings"]), ["401", "401k"])
+        self.assertTrue(all(u["tests"].values()))
+
+    def test_a_hold_now_is_adjudicated_by_the_unstable_history(self):
+        self.past(self.RUN)                                         # an earlier pass read 401k
+        e = self.ask(self.RUN, "I don't have a 401 ,", "have a 401k. I don't", "have a 401, I don't")
+        self.assertEqual((e["outcome"], e["relisten"]["verdict"]), ("no_difference", "hold"), e)   # 103 alone held
+        self.assertEqual(e["unstable_second_reading"]["verdict"], "pass")
+
+    def test_a_stable_disagreement_holds(self):
+        self.past("I don't have a 401 ,")
+        e = self.ask(self.RUN, "I don't have a 401 ,", "have a 401k. I don't", "have a 401, I don't")
+        self.assertEqual((e["outcome"], e["unstable_second_reading"]["verdict"]), ("hold", "hold"), e)
+        self.assertFalse(e["unstable_second_reading"]["tests"]["second_unstable"])
+        self.assertIn("ruling 105", e["reason"])
+
+    def test_a_different_number_holds_even_when_it_agrees_now(self):
+        run = "It cost them 68,000 dollars."
+        self.past("It cost them 86,000 dollars.")
+        e = self.ask(run, run)
+        self.assertEqual((e["outcome"], e["unstable_second_reading"]["verdict"]), ("hold", "hold"), e)
+        self.assertFalse(e["unstable_second_reading"]["tests"]["truncations_only"])
+
+    def test_a_different_name_holds_even_when_it_agrees_now(self):
+        run = "Then I asked Saylor about it."
+        self.past("Then I asked Taylor about it.")
+        e = self.ask(run, run)
+        self.assertEqual((e["outcome"], e["unstable_second_reading"]["verdict"]), ("hold", "hold"), e)
+
+    def test_another_audio_is_not_history(self):
+        self.past("I don't have a 401 ,", src="0" * 64)
+        e = self.ask(self.RUN, self.RUN)
+        self.assertEqual((e["outcome"], e["unstable_second_reading"]), ("no_difference", None), e)
+
+    def test_a_repeated_anchor_reads_the_token_at_the_windows_middle(self):   # audit batch 84 c1 (glm)
+        L = "i said a 401 and a 401k and a lot".split()
+        self.assertEqual(pinned.reading_near(L, 6, "and a 401 and a 401 and a".split()), "401")     # middle occurrence
+        self.assertEqual(pinned.reading_near(L, 6, "x y z".split()), "")                          # nothing anchors
+
+    def test_the_truncation_rule(self):
+        T = pinned.truncation_of
+        self.assertEqual([T("401k", "401"), T("68000", "680"), T("saylor", "say"), T("401k", ""), T("403b", "403")],
+                         [True, False, False, False, True])
+
+
